circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, located on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, spans 5. 281 kilometers and was designed by Hermann Tilke to host the Formula One season finale. Since 2009, the venue has served as the traditional closing round of the championship calendar, making it one of four Middle Eastern circuits on the modern F1 schedule.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Melbourne's Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling a lake in the city's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Australian Grand Prix and other major racing events each year. The venue maintains FIA Grade 1 certification and serves as the venue for several support series alongside its primary Formula One event.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The Red Bull Ring in Spielberg, Austria is a 4. 326 km circuit that originally operated as the Österreichring, hosting the Austrian Grand Prix continuously between 1970 and 1987. Following a redesign and renaming to the A1-Ring, the venue returned to the Formula One calendar from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital city, positioned along Baku Boulevard with a lap distance of 6. 003 km, ranking it as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The venue first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before transitioning to become the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017, with operations managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and has hosted the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the championship's inaugural Middle East venue. The FIA Grade 1 licensed track accommodates various motorsport disciplines including GP2 racing and 24-hour endurance events, with multiple circuit configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design with extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate nearly 141,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Belgian Walloon region near the town of Spa, this 7-kilometre circuit has been a fixture of Formula One racing since 1950, when it featured in the sport's inaugural season. The venue has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361-kilometre circuit serves as the home of the Canadian Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond F1, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships and open-wheel competitions throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in China's Jiading District is primarily recognized as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing events alongside its flagship Formula One race.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English circuit hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950 and has been the permanent home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, following decades of rotation with other venues. The track additionally serves as the venue for the British MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the first Formula One venue behind the Iron Curtain when it hosted its inaugural Grand Prix in 1986, commemorating Hungarian motorcycle racing pioneer János Drapál. Built in just eight months starting from late 1985, this 4. 381 km circuit was constructed near a major highway after authorities rejected plans for a street course through Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as one of the world's earliest purpose-built racing circuits. The venue has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its extended straightaways and fast-flowing corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit, a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport facility operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, serves as a premier venue for Formula One and Super Formula racing with a spectator capacity of 155,000.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that winds through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding thoroughfares alongside iconic venues such as Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas. The track traverses one of the world's most recognizable entertainment districts, featuring major hotels and casinos as key landscape elements throughout its layout.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named in tribute to two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate incidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The track has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix intermittently, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current layout, though it previously staged the race under different configurations until 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a specially constructed temporary circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 as the venue for the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches for 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, weaving around Monaco's harbor. Though formally named after Monaco itself, the track is widely known as Monte Carlo since the majority of its layout occupies that particular district of the principality.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: The Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km Dutch motorsport facility nestled in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam that hosts the Dutch Grand Prix. After a long absence, the track rejoined Formula One's schedule in 2021, though its hosting agreement with the sport concludes following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Grade 1 facility positioned north of Doha in Qatar, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a principal straight measuring 1. 068 kilometers.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The venue hosts Formula One racing and features an associated kart track bearing Ayrton Senna's name.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. Since 2021, it has been the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and it began hosting a Formula E race in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown and waterfront areas, creating a temporary racing layout that uses public roads around the Marina Bay district.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced combination of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it representative of modern circuit design. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA circuit hosting the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major racing series including NASCAR, MotoGP, and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance competition. The facility has previously accommodated various international motorsport events ranging from V8 Supercars to IndyCar racing.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, racing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships during his time with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 Grand Prix victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship and two Le Mans 24 Hours victories, making him the sole driver to have won both the Formula One drivers' title and the world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Italy in Formula One, driving for Mercedes since his 2025 entry into the sport. The driver has secured six Grand Prix victories during his early career.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he competes at the highest level of motorsport competition.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto is a Brazilian motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One as a driver for Audi.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One, having secured two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his tenure with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Across 13 seasons in the sport, Bottas has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One for Alpine, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan has appeared in seven Formula One races during the 2024-2025 season while holding a reserve role with Haas. Outside of his Formula One commitments, he races in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One, having previously achieved his sole grand prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France in the championship.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding a record-tying seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads in multiple statistical categories including race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved notable success in sportscars, claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, races for Ferrari in Formula One and has secured nine race victories over his nine-season career. He achieved runner-up status in the 2022 drivers' championship while competing for the Italian team.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate stints from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship as a BMW factory driver for WRT, alongside part-time NASCAR Cup Series commitments.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Across his eight-season career in the sport, he has claimed victory in 11 Grand Prix races.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. He previously achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez is a Mexican Formula One driver currently racing for Cadillac. The veteran competitor finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, currently races for McLaren in Formula One where he has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories over his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: An Australian driver who raced in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, Ricciardo earned the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his 14-season career in the sport. He achieved eight Grand Prix victories across his time competing at the top level of motorsport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, having secured four Grand Prix victories during his 12 seasons in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver competing in Formula One with the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda held a Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 and currently functions as a reserve driver for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag and has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, Verstappen has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently working as a reserve driver for the Cadillac Formula One team. He competed in the sport's top category from 2022 through 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have participated in Formula One competition.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, following its rebranding from Renault F1 Team to showcase the French marque's sports car division while maintaining works team status until Renault's 2025 exit. Alpine's only victory came through Esteban Ocon at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and the team currently operates with Mercedes power units and a French racing licence.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin represents British automotive heritage in Formula One through its current racing operation, AMR GP Limited, competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team designation.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished outfit, participating continuously in the championship since its inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially termed "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, remains the sport's oldest active competitor.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the squad commenced racing in 2016 after its establishment in 2014. Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had led the team since its inception.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970, initially built sports cars and achieved notable endurance racing success including the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours victory. After joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor, the team competed for over three decades before being purchased by Audi in 2024 and exiting the championship in 2025.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship arrangements. The team operates as part of the larger McLaren Group, with ultimate ownership held by Bahrain's state investment fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954 through both team ownership and engine supply. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas operation, based in Brackley and racing under a German licence, restructured its ownership in 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal stakeholder alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque is traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024 as one of Red Bull's two teams. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the squad operates alongside Red Bull Racing under Austrian ownership by Red Bull GmbH.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team structure. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, it operates as the second constructor under the Red Bull GmbH umbrella alongside Red Bull Racing.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian licence, has been a prominent Formula One outfit since its 2005 establishment by the Red Bull conglomerate. Christian Horner led the team through two decades of operations until his 2025 departure, with Laurent Mekies taking over as team principal. Red Bull GmbH also operates a second Formula One team, Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name in 2026 and operates from a substantial purpose-built facility.
